editorialTake:
AI is fragmenting into a hardware and service arms race, and luxury operators are about to feel the squeeze from both sides. Cerebras’s IPO, fresh off a $10 billion OpenAI deal and a tie-up with AWS, signals that AI is no longer just about software models, it is about who controls the chips that power them. Nvidia’s new AI models have sent quantum computing stocks soaring, while Google is pushing a new standard for how AI agents interact with users. The battle for AI dominance is shifting from code to silicon and from general-purpose to bespoke hardware.

Meanwhile, the old inflationary pressures are not going away. Gold futures hit $5,500 in January, with analysts warning of $6,000 before year-end. Jewellery margins are getting squeezed just as Kering’s latest results show even double-digit growth in jewellery cannot offset softness elsewhere. Amazon’s $10.8 billion acquisition of Globalstar to expand satellite internet is another signal: the giants are betting on infrastructure, not just content or distribution. In luxury, that means the cost of digital reach and physical goods is rising at both ends.

The strongest counterargument is that AI and hardware wars are still a step removed from daily retail, and that gold prices always fluctuate. But the pace and scale are different now. When OpenAI loses three senior executives at once, and Canva repositions itself as an AI platform, it is clear that the competitive ground is shifting fast.

For luxury and jewellery brands, the implication is clear: treat your tech stack and supply chain as strategic assets, not cost centers. Secure your access to AI tools and digital infrastructure now, before pricing power shifts further upstream. And with gold volatility set to continue, lock in margins with hedging or creative pricing. The winners will be those who can operate at both ends of the value chain, controlling the story, and the silicon it runs on.
oneSentenceSummary: Cerebras’s IPO hints that the AI hardware value chain is splintering, foreshadowing an era where bespoke chips dictate competitive advantage in AI services.
